correctness.rationale: For even q with fixed-point-free involution, the oriented target set consists of all q² fourmers T_{a,b}=ab bar(b) bar(a). Explicit suffix-prefix overlap analysis gives q/2 special two-target modules with reciprocal cost-one transitions and q(q-1)/2 ordinary modules with reciprocal cost-two transitions. All other intermodule transition costs are >=3. In a selected cyclic Hamiltonian ordering one must leave each module, adding excess one per ordinary module and two per special module above sum of cheap outcosts 2q²-q; the result is L_cyc>=(5q²-q)/2. For linear paths, omitting the last target exit and the corresponding module penalty yields L_lin>=L_cyc+1. The proof supplies a balanced connected directed multigraph of modules (loops within complement pairs and balanced pairs between distinct complement pairs); its Euler circuit traverses each module at its cheapest internal cost and connects modules at cost exactly 3, meeting the lower bound for every even q. Cutting one intermodule overlap yields the linear optimum. Independent reconstruction checked Euler covers for q=2,4,6,8 with lengths 9,38,87,156; q=4 literal Watson–Crick 38/39-word examples were checked to contain all 16 oriented targets. This finite evidence only corroborates the symbolic module/Euler proof.
